mediaWork.title: Framed: Astonishing True Stories of Wrongful Convictions
mediaWork.focusOrTheme: Collection of case studies examining wrongful convictions, their causes, and the fight for exoneration
mediaWork.summaryNotes: Collection of case studies examining wrongful convictions, their causes, and the fight for exoneration. Mentions 3,600 exonerations in the U.S. since 1989, with Centurion Ministries responsible for 70.
mediaWork.availabilityNotes: Hardcover, also available as paperback and e-book

mediaItem.itemTitle: Framed: Astonishing True Stories of Wrongful Convictions
mediaItem.focusOrTheme: Collection of case studies examining wrongful convictions, their causes, and the fight for exoneration
mediaItem.summaryNotes: Book examining ten true stories of wrongful convictions, their causes, and the fight for exoneration.
mediaItem.keyQuotes:
"From a moral perspective, it is imperative for a society to face and correct injustice... We decided to write about and focus on the ten most astonishing cases, and publish them as Framed. There are hundreds of others." — John Grisham
"The flaws and lethal errors that condemn innocent people in the American legal system have caused too many for too long to needlessly suffer." — Bryan Stevenson (quoted in book review)
"There have been 3,600 exonerations in the U.S. since 1989. In my understanding, there has not been one public inquiry about any single conviction." — Jim McCloskey

individuals.narrativeSummary: Wrongfully convicted of rape and murder of a 16-year-old White girl. Racial bias, tunnel vision, circumstantial evidence contributed to wrongful conviction. Died in 2018 of pneumonia.
Wrongfully convicted of murder of a local waitress. Lack of DNA testing at time of conviction contributed to wrongful conviction. Came within five days of execution.
